reasoning: Both attempts are correct and nearly identical. B wins narrowly because it puts ShowName right after NameOverride and ShowCount right after Count, and its short comments on units and on what turning off Centered does help the person using the panel.

criteria.note: All 13 controls get `Ordered(..., n)` inside their group, and each of the 4 groups is wrapped in `Ordered(ControlGroup({...}), n)`; no second argument is passed to ControlGroup.
The Content/State/Appearance/Story groups match the suggested split; Story = {Backdrop, Centered} keeps story-only settings apart from the tile's props.
Content 1, State 2, Appearance 3, Story 4, as requested.
Every read moves to `content.`, `state.`, `appearance.` or `storyControls.`, and StoryProps uses the same nesting.
Every Slider keeps its original arguments, the Choose list and all defaults are unchanged, and BlockTile.luau is untouched.
luau-lsp, selene and StyLua all pass.
Every control and each of the 4 groups uses `UILabs.Ordered(..., n)`, and ControlGroup gets only the controls table.
The Tile/State/Look/Preview groups are coherent; Preview = {Backdrop, Centered} holds the story-only settings.
Tile 1, State 2, Look 3, Preview 4; inside Tile, each toggle sits next to what it toggles (NameOverride then ShowName, Count then ShowCount).
All reads use `tile.`, `state.`, `look.` or `preview.`, and StoryProps matches the nesting.
Defaults and ranges are identical to the original, and BlockTile.luau is untouched.
luau-lsp, selene and StyLua all pass.

strengths: Complete and correct regrouping with order set at both levels
Comment explains that ControlGroup ignores an order argument
Clear local aliases for each group
weaknesses: Content group lists Count, ShowName, ShowCount, so ShowName is not next to NameOverride

strengths: Toggles placed next to the values they toggle
Helpful comments on pixel units and what turning off Centered does
weaknesses: No comment explaining why groups need Ordered (minor)
